Please keep the discussion on the mailing list rather than commenting on the wiki (wiki discussions get unwieldy fast).
Motivation
Today, the Producer'ssendOffsetsToTransaction(offsets, consumerGroupMetadata)allows EOS in read-process-write topologies that consume from regular consumer groups. With KIP-932 introducing share groups, the equivalent capability is missing for share groups.
Thisblocks share-group adoption in:
MirrorMaker and other Kafka-to-Kafka mirroring/forwarding pipelines.
Kafka Streams stateless topologies that want to use share groups for parallelism beyond partition count.
Atomic DLQ write in different connectors
The Goal: Atomic "Read-Process-Write"
EnableExactly-Once Semantics (EOS)by making acknowledgments part of a Kafka transaction.
Either the output is produced AND the source record is acknowledged, or neither happens. This KIP is scoped for Kafka producer write AND acknowledgements from a share group.
This KIP is focused on Kafka client applications which combine use of a KafkaProducer and a KafkaShareConsumer in the same application. It does not attempt enable EOS for share groups in processing frameworks such as Apache Flink.
Proposed Changes
This KIP introduces transactional share-group record acknowledgements. A new transactional share acknowledgement mode is introduced. Because Kafka transactions are driven by a Kafka producer, the application uses a KafkaProducer to begin and complete the transactions, along with KafkaShareConsumer to acknowledge the record deliveries. The combination of these classes achieves the transactional record acknowledgements.
Here's an example to illustrate:java
The notable parts are:
The share consumer is using the transactional share-acknowledgement mode.
The share consumer uses the producer to manage transaction context. (THIS PIECE STILL UNDER CONSTRUCTION)
If processing succeeds, the share consumer uses the ACCEPT acknowledge type, and commits the transaction.
If processing fails, the share consumer uses the REJECT acknowledge type, and commits the transaction.
If the transaction aborts, the acknowledgement will be rolled back which is semantically equivalent to the RELEASE acknowledgement type.
There are actually no new in-flight record states. Instead, the transition fromAcquiredtoAcknowledged(for ACCEPT) or toArchived(for REJECT) remains pending until the transaction completes.
There are several changes going on behind the scenes.
A new RPC TxnShareAcknowledge is used by the share consumer to tell the share-partition leader that records are being acknowledged transactionally.
When a share-partition is involved in a transaction, the partition of the_share_group_statetopic associated with its share-coordinator shard must be added to the transaction with the transaction coordinator so that the TC can write the transaction markers when the transaction closes. Even though the records being acknowledged are actually on a user's topic, it is the internal SGS topic which is added to the transaction because it is the state transition in the share coordinator (and then notified to the share-partition leader) which is transactional.
The share coordinator must be able to writeShareUpdaterecords marked with the producer ID and producer epoch corresponding to a transaction.
The share coordinator must be upgraded to replay transaction marker control records and update its internal state accordingly.
When a transaction completes, the share coordinator is responsible for notifying the share-partition leader of any share-partitions added to the transaction. This notification is via a new TxnComplete RPC sent from the share coordinator to the share-partition leader.
The share-partition leader is able to acknowledge records
